fix(hooks): resolve push-guard branch from cwd, stop false-matching quoted text

The push-guard hook resolved the current branch via CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR,
which is always the main checkout, never the worktree a session is
actually running in. With the main checkout sitting on main (the normal
state while work happens in a worktree), the hook denied every push,
including a feature branch pushed from its own worktree.

It also matched the push phrase inside quoted text and heredoc bodies --
a grep pattern or a file written via heredoc containing the phrase was
treated as an invocation, denying commands that never touched git.

Branch is now resolved from the hook input's own cwd (falling back to
CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR only when cwd is absent), and the command text is
run through a quote- and heredoc-aware stripper before the
command-position check, so quoted literals and heredoc bodies no
longer false-match while real invocations -- including one preceded by
env assignments or a shell separator -- are still caught.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5 <[redacted-email]>
EOF
)" 2>&1

tool_input.content:
#!/bin/bash
# Regression test for no-push-to-main.sh (beadle-fc6o).
#
# Builds a disposable git repo plus a worktree under TMPDIR (never this
# checkout), feeds crafted PreToolUse Bash hook JSON into the hook on stdin,
# and asserts on the permissionDecision in its output. Runs the whole suite
# twice: once with the real PATH (jq present) and once with jq hidden behind
# a PATH containing only a minimal, explicitly-allowlisted set of coreutils
# symlinks, so both the jq and the sed-fallback extraction paths are
# exercised end to end.
#
# Each case is self-contained: it sets up exactly the repo/branch/cwd state
# it needs, builds one JSON payload, runs the hook, and checks the single
# permissionDecision value in the hook's stdout (absent entirely when the
# hook allows, since it exits 0 with no output on allow).
set -u

SCRIPT_DIR=$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)
HOOK="$SCRIPT_DIR/no-push-to-main.sh"

FAILURES=0
CASES=0

# A disposable TMPDIR-rooted workspace for this whole run: one shared repo
# plus worktree, reused across cases that only need the branch/path state it
# already provides, and a per-case JSON payload file.
WORKDIR=$(mktemp -d)
trap 'rm -rf "$WORKDIR"' EXIT

REPO="$WORKDIR/repo"
WORKTREE="$WORKDIR/wt-feat"

git init -q -b main "$REPO"
git -C "$REPO" config user.email "[redacted-email]"
git -C "$REPO" config user.name "Test"
printf 'hello\n' >"$REPO/README.md"
git -C "$REPO" add README.md
git -C "$REPO" commit -q -m "init"
git -C "$REPO" worktree add -q -b feat/example "$WORKTREE"

# A PATH containing only explicitly-named coreutils (no jq), built from
# absolute symlinks so a shell function wrapping a tool on the real PATH
# (e.g. a `grep` alias) cannot leak through. Exercises the hook's sed-based
# command/cwd extraction fallback.
NOJQ_BIN="$WORKDIR/nojq-bin"
mkdir -p "$NOJQ_BIN"
for tool in bash sh grep sed cat printf git dirname basename mktemp rm \
            chmod mkdir tr head find xargs awk cut; do
    tool_path=$(command -v "$tool" 2>/dev/null) || continue
    ln -sf "$(readlink -f "$tool_path")" "$NOJQ_BIN/$tool"
done

# json_payload COMMAND CWD > file -- builds a one-line JSON hook payload.
# Uses python3 -I (isolated mode, no site/user customization) purely as a
# JSON encoder so embedded quotes, backslashes, and newlines in COMMAND are
# escaped correctly; this never executes untrusted code, only serializes two
# known-safe local strings.
json_payload() {
    local command="$1" cwd="$2"
    python3 -I -c '
import json, sys
print(json.dumps({"tool_input": {"command": sys.argv[1]}, "cwd": sys.argv[2]}))
' "$command" "$cwd"
}

# run_hook PATH_OVERRIDE PAYLOAD_FILE PROJECT_DIR -- invokes the hook with a
# given PATH (real or the no-jq allowlist) and CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR, returns its
# stdout.
run_hook() {
    local path_override="$1" payload_file="$2" project_dir="$3"
    PATH="$path_override" CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR="$project_dir" bash "$HOOK" <"$payload_file"
}

# assert_decision DESC PATH_LABEL PATH_OVERRIDE COMMAND CWD PROJECT_DIR WANT
# WANT is "deny" or "allow". Builds the payload, runs the hook, and checks
# whether a deny payload appeared.
assert_decision() {
    local desc="$1" path_label="$2" path_override="$3" command="$4" cwd="$5" \
        project_dir="$6" want="$7"
    CASES=$((CASES + 1))

    local payload_file
    payload_file=$(mktemp)
    json_payload "$command" "$cwd" >"$payload_file"

    local output
    output=$(run_hook "$path_override" "$payload_file" "$project_dir")
    rm -f "$payload_file"

    local got="allow"
    if printf '%s' "$output" | grep -q '"permissionDecision":"deny"'; then
        got="deny"
    fi

    if [[ "$got" == "$want" ]]; then
        printf 'PASS [%s] %s\n' "$path_label" "$desc"
    else
        printf 'FAIL [%s] %s: want=%s got=%s output=%s\n' \
            "$path_label" "$desc" "$want" "$got" "$output"
        FAILURES=$((FAILURES + 1))
    fi
}

run_suite() {
    local path_label="$1" path_override="$2"

    # Worktree case: pushing a feature branch from its own worktree, while
    # the main checkout sits on main, is allowed. This is the branch the hook
    # used to resolve via CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR (always the main checkout) and
    # deny outright.
    assert_decision "push feature branch from its own worktree" \
        "$path_label" "$path_override" \
        "git push origin feat/example" "$WORKTREE" "$REPO" "allow"

    # cwd on main is still denied, regardless of what CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR says.
    assert_decision "push while cwd is on main" \
        "$path_label" "$path_override" \
        "git push origin feat/example" "$REPO" "$REPO" "deny"

    # A push whose destination ref is main/master is denied even from a
    # feature-branch worktree.
    assert_decision "push targeting main from a feature-branch worktree" \
        "$path_label" "$path_override" \
        "git push origin main" "$WORKTREE" "$REPO" "deny"

    assert_decision "push targeting master via full ref from a worktree" \
        "$path_label" "$path_override" \
        "git push origin HEAD:refs/heads/master" "$WORKTREE" "$REPO" "deny"

    # The push phrase inside a single-quoted argument of a non-git command
    # (grep) is data, not an invocation, and must be allowed.
    assert_decision "push phrase in single-quoted grep pattern" \
        "$path_label" "$path_override" \
        "grep -n 'git push' foo.sh" "$WORKTREE" "$REPO" "allow"

    # Same, double-quoted, inside an unrelated echo.
    assert_decision "push phrase in double-quoted echo argument" \
        "$path_label" "$path_override" \
        'echo "please do not git push to main"' "$WORKTREE" "$REPO" "allow"

    # The push phrase (even naming main) inside a heredoc body written to a
    # file is prose, not an invocation, and must be allowed.
    assert_decision "push phrase inside a heredoc body" \
        "$path_label" "$path_override" \
        "$(printf "cat <<'EOF' > foo.md\ngit push origin main is blocked by policy\nEOF\n")" \
        "$WORKTREE" "$REPO" "allow"

    # A real invocation preceded by env assignments is still detected and,
    # since the destination is main, denied.
    assert_decision "env-prefixed real push to main is denied" \
        "$path_label" "$path_override" \
        "GIT_TRACE=1 git push origin main" "$WORKTREE" "$REPO" "deny"

    # A real invocation after a shell separator, in a compound command, is
    # still detected (and allowed here since the destination is a feature
    # branch).
    assert_decision "compound command with real push to feature branch" \
        "$path_label" "$path_override" \
        "cd foo && git push origin feat/example" "$WORKTREE" "$REPO" "allow"

    # A quoted occurrence of the full push-to-main phrase sitting alongside a
    # genuine push to a feature branch must not cause a false deny -- the
    # quoted text is inert, the real invocation's own destination governs.
    assert_decision "quoted push-to-main phrase beside a real feature push" \
        "$path_label" "$path_override" \
        "grep 'git push origin main' x.sh; git push origin feat/example" \
        "$WORKTREE" "$REPO" "allow"
}

run_suite "jq" "$PATH"
run_suite "no-jq" "$NOJQ_BIN"

echo "no-push-to-main_test.sh: ${CASES} cases, ${FAILURES} failures"
if [[ "$FAILURES" -gt 0 ]]; then
    exit 1
fi
exit 0
